name: Advanced DAX: calculation groups, TREATAS, semi-additive, virtual tables

why.matters: Advanced DAX patterns are how one certified model answers hundreds of questions without hundreds of near-duplicate measures.
why.failure: A semi-additive stock measure sums weekly snapshots and inventory looks ten times larger than it is.
why.use: Calculation groups for repeated transformations (time intelligence, currency); window functions for running totals and comparisons.
why.avoid: Clever DAX that nobody else on the team can maintain. Prefer visual calculations for one-off visual math.

verified.context: Calculation groups, window functions, visual calculations docs, Sept 2026

steps: Stock On Hand = CALCULATE(SUM(FactInventory[QuantityOnHand]), LASTDATE(FactInventory[SnapshotDate])) — put it in a matrix by MonthName. Notice it uses the last snapshot date within each month.

Now the problem: LASTDATE over Dates gives blank for days with no snapshot. Rewrite with LASTNONBLANK: CALCULATE(SUM(QuantityOnHand), LASTNONBLANK(Dates[Date], CALCULATE(SUM(FactInventory[QuantityOnHand])))).
asg.exp: Matrix by month shows the last week's level, not a sum. Below Reorder flags Hydro Filter Bottle at the end of January and Ridge Runner Boots at the end of February (both under their reorder point of 30); nothing is below reorder at the end of March.

steps: Tabular Editor 2 → New Calculation Group "Time Calc" with items: Current = SELECTEDMEASURE(), PM = CALCULATE(SELECTEDMEASURE(), DATEADD(Dates[Date], -1, MONTH)), MoM % = DIVIDE(SELECTEDMEASURE() - CALCULATE(SELECTEDMEASURE(), DATEADD(Dates[Date], -1, MONTH)), CALCULATE(SELECTEDMEASURE(), DATEADD(Dates[Date], -1, MONTH))), MTD = CALCULATE(SELECTEDMEASURE(), DATESMTD(Dates[Date])).
Set a format string expression on MoM % to "0.0%" and on the others to SELECTEDMEASUREFORMATSTRING().
Save to the model. Matrix: rows Category, columns Time Calc, values Net Sales, then switch value to Orders. Both get all four variants without new measures.
Set precedence and observe what happens when you add a second calculation group "Currency" (below).
asg.exp: Format strings switch correctly per column. Implicit measures stop working (turn on Discourage implicit measures).

steps: Relate ExchangeRates to Dates on RateDate (inactive is fine). Build a rate lookup measure: Rate = VAR c = SELECTEDVALUE(Currency[Code]) VAR dte = MAX(Dates[Date]) RETURN CALCULATE(MAX(ExchangeRates[RateToUSD]), ExchangeRates[Currency] = c, ExchangeRates[RateDate] <= dte, LASTDATE(...)) — or a simpler LASTNONBLANK pattern.
Calculation group "Currency": USD = SELECTEDMEASURE(), Selected = SUMX(VALUES(Dates[Date]), CALCULATE(SELECTEDMEASURE()) / [Rate]) where Rate is the last known rate for that date.
Currency slicer from a disconnected table. Check Net Sales in EUR for January.
asg.exp: Converting per day then summing gives a different number than converting the monthly total by one rate; you can explain which is correct.

steps: Delete the DimCategory relationship to FactBudget from the Intermediate model.
Budget via TREATAS = CALCULATE(SUM(FactBudget[BudgetAmount]), TREATAS(VALUES(DimProduct[Category]), FactBudget[Category]), TREATAS(VALUES(Dates[YearMonth]), FactBudget[YearMonth])).
Compare against the physical relationship version in DAX Studio timings.
Do the same with CROSSFILTER to temporarily change a relationship direction inside a measure.
asg.exp: Same numbers; TREATAS is slower on large budgets but has no model impact.

steps: Customer ABC Class = VAR t = ADDCOLUMNS(ALLSELECTED(DimCustomer[CustomerKey]), "@s", [Net Sales]) VAR total = SUMX(t, [@s]) VAR cur = [Net Sales] VAR cum = SUMX(FILTER(t, [@s] >= cur), [@s]) RETURN SWITCH(TRUE(), DIVIDE(cum,total) <= 0.7, "A", DIVIDE(cum,total) <= 0.9, "B", "C").
Rewrite the running total with WINDOW: Running Sales = CALCULATE([Net Sales], WINDOW(1, ABS, 0, REL, ALLSELECTED(DimCustomer[CustomerName]), ORDERBY([Net Sales], DESC))).
Use OFFSET to get the previous customer's sales in a sorted table, and RANK for the position.
Explain in a comment why WINDOW cannot be wrapped in a non-trivial FILTER.
asg.exp: A/B/C classification sums to 100% of customers; Running Sales in the last row equals the total.

int.q: Calculation group precedence: what does it decide?
int.a: When two groups apply to the same cell, the higher-precedence group's expression is applied last (outermost). Time intelligence normally wraps currency conversion, so Time Calc gets higher precedence.

int.q: LASTDATE vs LASTNONBLANK vs MAX for semi-additive measures.
int.a: LASTDATE returns the last date in the current date filter even if there is no data. LASTNONBLANK scans for the last date where the expression is non-blank. MAX(date) is faster than LASTDATE but returns a scalar, so wrap it in a filter. Prefer LASTNONBLANKVALUE for a single column.

TREATAS is per-measure and has no model change; relationships are global and faster. TREATAS handles multi-column mappings with no key. Relationships propagate RLS; TREATAS does not filter other measures automatically.
Calculation items that return the base measure should keep its format; without it every item defaults to the group's format string and Net Sales loses its $.

int.q: When do window functions (WINDOW, OFFSET, INDEX, RANK) beat the classic EARLIER / FILTER patterns?
int.a: Whenever you need ordered access (previous row, running total, top-N within group). They are optimised for it and readable; the classic patterns are O(n²) iterators.

int.q: How do you handle a currency conversion where the rate is missing for a date?
int.a: Use the last known rate before that date (LASTNONBLANK pattern or a forward-fill in Power Query). Surface missing rates as a data-quality measure rather than silently returning blank.

o: Are ignored by calculation items and should be disabled
ass.why: Calculation items only apply to explicit measures; discourage implicit measures in the model.
